html:
The Hunnic Empire was the realm of the Huns, nomads from the steppe east of the Volga who built a short-lived empire north of the Danube in the late 4th and 5th centuries. It reached its height under Attila, from 434 to 453.

The Huns crossed into Europe around 370. They broke the Alans and the Goths north of the Black Sea and set off a chain of moves. Fleeing Goths crossed the Danube into the Roman Empire in 376. By the 430s the Huns ruled the Hungarian plain and many subject peoples: Goths, Gepids, Sarmatians and others.

Under Attila and his brother Bleda, and then Attila alone:

  • They raided the Eastern Roman Empire and forced Constantinople to pay large sums of gold.
  • In 451 they invaded Gaul and were stopped at the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains by Romans under Aetius and the Visigoths.
  • In 452 they invaded Italy, then withdrew.

Attila died in 453. His sons fought over the inheritance, and the subject peoples rose and beat them at the Battle of Nedao around 454. The last Hun king of note, Dengizich, was killed in 469.

The Huns left almost no writing of their own. Their language is unknown, and any link to the Xiongnu of Mongolia is unproven. Their real legacy was indirect: the pressure they put on Germanic peoples helped bring down the Western Roman Empire.
